_comment: ClawFactory egress policy. Root-owned, /etc/clawfactory/egress-policy.json, root:root 0644.
TWO SECTIONS.
read_fetch   -- research destinations the agent may fetch from. Carried here so that
Guard 3 becomes a day of config plus UI rather than a second full guard.
NOTHING IN v1 ENFORCES THIS SECTION. It is declarative only. Do not
describe it as a control until Guard 3 wires it up.
send_actions -- approval-gated destinations. Guard 2 DOES enforce this section.
send_actions IS EMPTY BY DEFAULT AND THAT IS THE FAIL-CLOSED STATE. No destination is
permitted until the user configures SMTP in Studio, which is the act that authorizes
exactly one host and port. A fresh install can enqueue nothing and send nothing.
HOW send_actions IS ENFORCED, stated precisely because the wrong description is easy to
write and hard to unwrite. The send broker reads this file and refuses any destination
not listed here. That is BROKER-ENFORCED, in root-owned code reading a root-owned file.
It is NOT firewall-enforced. The nft chain begins `meta skuid != 1000 return`, which
leaves every non-1000 uid unfiltered by construction, so the broker's ability to reach
SMTP is emergent rather than granted. There is no firewall exemption for the broker and
none should ever be added.
It remains structural with respect to the AGENT, because the agent cannot modify
root-owned code or this file. Matching is exact on host and port. No wildcards: a
wildcard in a send destination is an exfiltration channel with a friendly name.

read_fetch._note: Declarative only in v1. Guard 3 consumes this; nothing enforces it today.
